## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.

Restore the bundled defaults before merge because the existing loader now fails when called. Port validation and configuration error reporting also need correction; test coverage was assessed by reading the tests.

## Changes
The pull request adds millisecond timeout parsing, port validation, configuration loading, and host normalization with tests. It also deletes the bundled defaults and adds reviewer documentation and a review fixture.

## Critical
- app/defaults.json:1 [base] — correctness — Restore the bundled defaults file — Calling `load_defaults()` now raises `FileNotFoundError` instead of returning `{"timeout": 30}`. Deleting this file leaves the reader at app/startup.py:6 pointing to a nonexistent sibling. — Any caller loading the bundled defaults fails before it can use the default configuration.

## Important
- app/parse.py:22 — correctness — Include port 65535 in the valid range — Passing `65535` returns `False`, although the documented usable range includes it. The strict upper comparison excludes that endpoint. — Callers relying on this validator reject configurations using the highest valid TCP port.
- app/parse.py:30 — silent-failure — Expose configuration loading failures — A missing file, denied read, or malformed JSON returns `{}` without identifying the failure. The broad `except Exception` also hides unexpected loader errors. — Callers cannot distinguish an empty configuration from a failed load or determine which configuration problem to correct.
- app/parse.py:40 — tests — Exercise trailing-dot host normalization — For `"Example.COM."`, the new trailing-dot branch is untested. `test_normalize_host_lowercases` supplies `"Example.COM"`, so removing suffix stripping would leave every existing test passing. — A regression can retain the trailing dot while the host-normalization tests continue to pass.

## Suggestions
- app/parse.py:35 — comments — Align the empty-host documentation and behavior — For `normalize_host("")`, the docstring promises “returns None when h is empty”, but the branch executes `return ""`. — Callers following the documented sentinel contract can mistake an empty host for a normalized value.
